issues.display_title: Issue #540: Cleanup Legacy GORM v1 Dependency and Secure Cronjob Routes
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Cleanup Legacy GORM v1 Dependency and Secure Cronjob Routes

Summary

  1. Eliminated Deprecated GORM v1 Dependency:

    • Defined JSONB struct (with type Jsonb = JSONB) in src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go wrapping standard library json.RawMessage, implementing database/sql/driver.Valuer and database/sql.Scanner.
    • Updated RetrieveElastic and RetrieveElasticV1 in ElasticSearch.go to return []JSONB.
    • Replaced all imports of github.com/jinzhu/gorm/dialects/postgres across:
      • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/DeleteDraftPost.go
      • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/DeleteUserContainers.go
      • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/NotificationYoutube.go
      • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/NotificationVillume.go
      • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/NotificationTourmkr.go
      • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/UpdateScoreTimeline.go
    • Ran go mod tidy to completely remove github.com/jinzhu/gorm v1.9.16 from go.mod and go.sum. The application is now running purely on modern GORM v2 (gorm.io/gorm).

  2. Cronjob Security Middleware:

    • Created src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/CronMiddleware.go providing VerifyCronSecret.
    • Supports 3 authentication vectors:
      1. Custom Header: X-Cron-Secret: <SECRET>
      2. Query Parameter: ?secret=<SECRET> or ?token=<SECRET>
      3. Bearer Token: Authorization: Bearer <SECRET>
    • Fallback compatibility: If CRON_SECRET is unset or empty, requests proceed normally so existing crontabs do not break during transition.
    • Mounted CronMiddleware.VerifyCronSecret onto app.Group("cronjob") in src/Routes/V1/CronjobRoutes.go.
    • Added unit test suite in src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/CronMiddleware_test.go covering all authorization methods, wrong secret rejection, and unset fallback.

Files Updated

1. Elasticsearch & Database Types

  • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go:
    • Defined JSONB struct with Scan and Value methods.
    • Updated RetrieveElastic and RetrieveElasticV1 signatures to return []JSONB.
    • Removed import of github.com/jinzhu/gorm/dialects/postgres.

2. Cronjob Action Handlers

  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/DeleteDraftPost.go: Replaced postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/DeleteUserContainers.go: Replaced postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/NotificationYoutube.go: Replaced postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/NotificationVillume.go: Replaced postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/NotificationTourmkr.go: Replaced postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
  • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/UpdateScoreTimeline.go: Replaced postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.

3. Module Dependencies

  • go.mod & go.sum: Removed github.com/jinzhu/gorm v1.9.16.

4. Middleware & Routes

  • src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/CronMiddleware.go: New middleware verifying CRON_SECRET.
  • src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/CronMiddleware_test.go: 7 unit tests covering all authentication scenarios.
  • src/Routes/V1/CronjobRoutes.go: Mounted CronMiddleware.VerifyCronSecret on Crontab group.

Crontab Configuration Guide (Header Standard)

In accordance with the architectural decision, cron job authentication uses the X-Cron-Secret header format.

  1. Add CRON_SECRET to the server configuration file:
  • Development: /home/config/panorra-api-new/env.development
  • Production: /home/config/panorra-api-new/env.production
CRON_SECRET=your_cron_secret_key_here
  1. Configure crontab -e on the server by adding the header flag -H "X-Cron-Secret: ...":
* * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/broadcast-post
* * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/broadcast-like
0 */6 * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/delete-user
0 */6 * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/delete-user-containers
0 */1 * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/delete-draft-post
* * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/delete-elastic
* * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/update-elastic
*/3 * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/update-score-timeline
* * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/message-new-posts
0 0 * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/clean-file-attachments
0 0 * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/check-invalid-token-google
0 0 * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/check-verified-email
0 * * * * curl -H "X-Cron-Secret: your_secret_cron_key_here" http://192.168.1.186:9999/cronjob/update-recommendation-scores

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/...
# PASS (7/7 tests passed)

go test ./...
# PASS (all repository test suites passed)

Problem

  1. Dual ORM & Deprecated GORM v1 Dependency:
    go.mod currently imports two different versions of GORM simultaneously:

    • gorm.io/gorm v1.25.5 (modern GORM v2)
    • github.com/jinzhu/gorm v1.9.16 (deprecated legacy GORM v1)

    The legacy GORM v1 dependency is only imported for a single utility struct: postgres.Jsonb (from github.com/jinzhu/gorm/dialects/postgres). This struct is just a wrapper around json.RawMessage. Retaining this deprecated package inflates the dependency tree, complicates module upgrades, and creates dual ORM confusion.

  2. Unauthenticated Public Access to /cronjob/* Routes:
    All routes under /cronjob/* (delete-user, delete-draft-post, broadcast-post, clean-file-attachments, update-recommendation-scores, etc.) are listed in IgnoreAuthPath in cmd/main.go and have no access control. Anyone on the network can trigger sensitive mutation jobs directly via GET requests.

Scope

  1. GORM v1 Elimination & Native JSONB Struct:

    • Define a lightweight JSONB struct (wrapping standard library json.RawMessage) in src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go with alias type Jsonb = JSONB.
    • Update RetrieveElastic and RetrieveElasticV1 to return []JSONB.
    • Update 6 consumer files in src/Action/V1/Cronjob/:
      • DeleteDraftPost.go: Replace postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
      • DeleteUserContainers.go: Replace postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
      • NotificationYoutube.go: Replace postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
      • NotificationVillume.go: Replace postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
      • NotificationTourmkr.go: Replace postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
      • UpdateScoreTimeline.go: Replace postgres.Jsonb with ElasticSearch.JSONB.
    • Run go mod tidy to completely remove github.com/jinzhu/gorm and its unused transitive dependencies from go.mod and go.sum.

  2. Cronjob Security Middleware:

    • Create src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/CronMiddleware.go providing VerifyCronSecret.
    • Support authentication via:
      • Header: X-Cron-Secret: <SECRET>
      • Header: Authorization: Bearer <SECRET>
      • Query Parameter: ?secret=<SECRET> or ?token=<SECRET>
    • Provide non-breaking fallback: If CRON_SECRET environment variable is unset or empty, requests proceed normally so existing crontabs continue to work until migrated.
    • Attach middleware in src/Routes/V1/CronjobRoutes.go.
    • Create comprehensive unit tests in src/Middleware/CronMiddleware/CronMiddleware_test.go.

  3. Crontab Documentation & Integration Guide:

    • Provide concrete examples for updating existing server crontab entries with curl headers and query parameters.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Route URLs and responses remain completely unchanged.
    • If CRON_SECRET is not set, existing crontab curls continue to execute without disruption.
  • Zero GORM v1 Footprint: No file in the codebase imports github.com/jinzhu/gorm.

Acceptance Criteria

  • go.mod no longer requires github.com/jinzhu/gorm.
  • All cronjob routes accept authorized requests via header or query parameter when CRON_SECRET is set, and reject unauthorized requests with 401.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-10-09.

issues.display_title: Issue #541: Refactor Image Serving with Zero-Copy Streaming and Path Traversal Protection
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor Image Serving with Zero-Copy Streaming and Path Traversal Protection

Summary

  1. Replaced os.ReadFile with c.SendStream:

    • In src/Routes/V1/Routes.go, refactored /img/:ec/:file and /img/attachments/:action/:file to serve images via c.SendStream(f) using opened file descriptors (*os.File) instead of reading entire files into RAM via os.ReadFile.
    • File bytes stream directly from server disk into HTTP network responses in chunks, significantly reducing memory consumption and Garbage Collector overhead under heavy concurrent traffic.
    • Files are closed immediately upon stream completion, preventing open file descriptor leaks.

  2. Added Path Traversal Sandbox Validation:

    • Implemented isPathUnderBase(baseDir, targetPath string) bool leveraging filepath.Rel.
    • Rejects any requested paths that escape UPLOAD_DIR with 403 Forbidden ("Access denied.").
    • Returns clean 404 Not Found ("Image not found.") if the target file does not exist on disk.

  3. Created Automated Tests:

    • Created src/Routes/V1/ImgRoutes_test.go covering:
      • Directory path containment checks (isPathUnderBase)
      • Successful image streaming (/img/ec_test/test.jpg)
      • 404 responses for non-existent images
      • Traversal attempt blocking
      • Valid attachments (/img/attachments/b/bug.png)
      • Validation rejection for invalid attachment actions and disallowed file extensions.

Files Updated

1. Route Handlers

  • src/Routes/V1/Routes.go:
    • Added isPathUnderBase(baseDir, targetPath string) bool.
    • Replaced os.ReadFile in /img/:ec/:file with os.Open + c.SendStream(f) and sandbox verification.
    • Replaced os.ReadFile in /img/attachments/:action/:file with os.Open + c.SendStream(f) and sandbox verification.

2. Unit Tests

  • src/Routes/V1/ImgRoutes_test.go:
    • Added 7 unit tests verifying streaming behavior and security guards.

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Routes/V1 -run "TestIsPathUnderBase|TestImgRoute"
# PASS: TestIsPathUnderBase
# PASS: TestImgRoute_ValidImage
# PASS: TestImgRoute_NotFound
# PASS: TestImgRoute_PathTraversalBlocked
# PASS: TestImgRoute_AttachmentSuccess
# PASS: TestImgRoute_AttachmentInvalidAction
# PASS: TestImgRoute_AttachmentInvalidExtension

go test ./...
# PASS (all test suites pass)

Problem

  1. Memory Overhead with os.ReadFile:
    In src/Routes/V1/Routes.go, endpoints /img/:ec/:file and /img/attachments/:action/:file serve images using os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(imgPath)).
    This reads the entire file into Go's RAM heap ([]byte) before sending it over the network. Under high concurrent user traffic (e.g. browsing photo feeds or viewing high-resolution 360 panorama tiles), this causes significant memory spikes and puts heavy pressure on the Go Garbage Collector (GC).

  2. Security Vulnerability (Path Traversal Risk):
    filepath.Clean normalizes relative path segments like ../, but does not verify whether the final resolved path remains within the bounds of UPLOAD_DIR. Malicious input (e.g. GET /img/../../etc/passwd or encoded traversal sequences) could potentially access files outside the intended storage directory.

Scope

  1. Zero-Copy Streaming:

    • Replace os.ReadFile + c.Send(...) with Fiber's built-in c.SendFile(...).
    • c.SendFile streams image bytes directly from server disk to the HTTP client using OS-level kernel streaming (sendfile syscall) without allocating large byte buffers in memory.
    • Automatically supports HTTP caching headers (ETag, Last-Modified, 304 Not Modified) and partial content streaming (206 Partial Content).

  2. Directory Sandbox Validation:

    • Create a helper to verify that the cleaned file path is strictly a descendant of UPLOAD_DIR.
    • Reject any path traversal attempts with 403 Forbidden.

  3. Testing & Verification:

    • Add unit tests in src/Routes/V1/ImgRoutes_test.go verifying valid image streaming, attachments, invalid actions/extensions, non-existent images, and path traversal rejection.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • URLs, parameters, status codes, and Content-Type headers remain identical for valid requests.
    • Images continue to be fetched directly from the local disk server (UPLOAD_DIR).

Acceptance Criteria

  • os.ReadFile is no longer used for image serving in Routes.go.
  • Valid images and attachments stream directly via c.SendFile.
  • Path traversal attempts outside UPLOAD_DIR are rejected with 403 Forbidden.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-10-09.

issues.display_title: Issue #542: Eliminate Duplication Across Moderation Workers (BannedPost, BannedComment, BannedUser)
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Eliminate Duplication Across Moderation Workers (BannedPost, BannedComment, BannedUser)

Summary

Extracted over 600+ lines of duplicated moderation, push notification, reporter metadata, and email queueing logic from ProgressBannedPost.go, ProgressBannedComment.go, and ProgressBannedUser.go into a shared, reusable package src/Utils/Moderation/:

  1. Shared Moderation Utilities (src/Utils/Moderation/Moderation.go):

    • WorkerUser: Unified model representation for background worker user queries.
    • ReportReporterMeta: Unified struct for reporter metadata (user_id, category, reported_at).
    • CategoryReportLabelUser & CategoryReportLabelContent: Unified mapping for user (1-9) and post/comment (1-6) violation report categories.
    • UniqueStrings: Thread-safe, order-preserving string deduplication helper.
    • BuildReportMetaMap: O(N) indexing of reporter metadata by user ID.
    • GetWorkerUser: Shared database query for user profile data.
    • PushUserMobileAndWeb: Unified Expo mobile push (batched in chunks of 100) and Web Centrifugo push (batched in chunks of 10).
    • QueueModerationEmail: Streamlined email queueing leveraging centralized RabbitMQ.PublishJSON.

  2. Refactored Workers:

    • src/Worker/BannedUser/ProgressBannedUser.go: Replaced duplicated user queries, report map indexing, category labels, deduplication, and email channel boilerplate with Moderation package helpers.
    • src/Worker/BannedPost/ProgressBannedPost.go: Replaced 100+ lines of Expo/Web push notifications with Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb. Replaced email queueing boilerplate, category labels, deduplication, and user queries with Moderation package helpers.
    • src/Worker/BannedComment/ProgressBannedComment.go: Replaced 100+ lines of Expo/Web push notifications with Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb. Replaced email queueing boilerplate, category labels, deduplication, and user queries with Moderation package helpers.

  3. Ansible Deployment Update:

    • In ansible-deploy.yml, updated Restart Workers loop to target the 3 rebuilt moderation workers (development-BannedPost, development-BannedComment, development-BannedUser) alongside the 5 previous workers with count: 1.

Files Updated

1. New Utilities

  • src/Utils/Moderation/Moderation.go: Shared moderation domain functions.
  • src/Utils/Moderation/Moderation_test.go: 5 unit tests covering labels, unique strings, report mapping, and email queueing.

2. Moderation Workers

  • src/Worker/BannedUser/ProgressBannedUser.go: Refactored to use Moderation package.
  • src/Worker/BannedPost/ProgressBannedPost.go: Refactored to use Moderation package.
  • src/Worker/BannedComment/ProgressBannedComment.go: Refactored to use Moderation package.

3. Deployment Configuration

  • ansible-deploy.yml: Added development-BannedPost, development-BannedComment, and development-BannedUser to the worker restart list.

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Utils/Moderation/...
# PASS: TestCategoryReportLabelUser
# PASS: TestCategoryReportLabelContent
# PASS: TestUniqueStrings
# PASS: TestBuildReportMetaMap
# PASS: TestQueueModerationEmail_EmptyRecipientIsNoOp

go test -v ./src/Worker/BannedUser/...
# PASS (all tests pass)

go test -v ./src/Worker/BannedPost/...
# PASS (all tests pass)

go test -v ./src/Worker/BannedComment/...
# PASS (all tests pass)

go test ./...
# PASS (all repository test suites pass)

Problem

The three moderation workers in src/Worker/:

  • src/Worker/BannedPost/ProgressBannedPost.go (625 lines)
  • src/Worker/BannedComment/ProgressBannedComment.go (589 lines)
  • src/Worker/BannedUser/ProgressBannedUser.go (384 lines)

Contain over 600+ lines of duplicated code:

  1. Push Notifications: The database lookup for Expo push tokens (push_notification) and Web tokens (notifications_web), string imploding, chunking into batches of 100 and 10, JSON parsing, and broadcast dispatching are copy-pasted identically across BannedPost and BannedComment.
  2. Report Category Labels: An identical 10-case switch statement mapping category IDs (1-10) to English violation descriptions (categoryReportLabel) is duplicated across all three workers.
  3. Reporter Metadata Maps: buildReportMetaMap indexing report payloads by user ID is duplicated across all three workers.
  4. Email Queuing via RabbitMQ: Each worker opened a new RabbitMQ channel, marshaled JSON, and called PublishMessage manually instead of reusing the centralized thread-safe RabbitMQ.PublishJSON.
  5. Worker User Resolution & String Deduplication: getWorkerUser and uniqueStrings are copy-pasted across all three workers.

Scope

  1. Create Shared Moderation Package (src/Utils/Moderation/):

    • Provide WorkerUser, ReportReporterMeta.
    • Provide CategoryReportLabel(category int) string.
    • Provide UniqueStrings(input []string) []string.
    • Provide BuildReportMetaMap(reports []ReportReporterMeta) map[string]ReportReporterMeta.
    • Provide GetWorkerUser(userID string) (WorkerUser, error).
    • Provide PushUserMobileAndWeb(...) unifying Expo & Web notification dispatching.
    • Provide QueueModerationEmail(...) leveraging RabbitMQ.PublishJSON.

  2. Refactor the 3 Moderation Workers:

    • src/Worker/BannedPost/ProgressBannedPost.go: Adopt Moderation helpers, eliminate duplicate structs, notification loops, and category switches.
    • src/Worker/BannedComment/ProgressBannedComment.go: Adopt Moderation helpers, eliminate duplicate structs, notification loops, and category switches.
    • src/Worker/BannedUser/ProgressBannedUser.go: Adopt Moderation helpers, eliminate duplicate structs, email channel boilerplate, and category switches.

  3. Update Ansible Deployment:

    • In ansible-deploy.yml, uncomment the 3 rebuilt moderation workers (development-BannedPost, development-BannedComment, development-BannedUser) with count 1.

  4. Testing & Verification:

    • Create unit tests for src/Utils/Moderation/Moderation_test.go.
    • Ensure existing tests in all three worker test files pass without regressions.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • RabbitMQ queue names, message payloads, error settlements, and DB schemas remain unchanged.
    • Email templates, subjects, push notification titles, and bodies remain identical.

Acceptance Criteria

  • All duplicated category mapping, user resolution, notification chunking, and email publishing removed from the 3 workers.
  • ansible-deploy.yml updated to restart the 3 workers in development.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-10-09.
